views.title: From profile to native session
views.description: Choose the client you want to use. The profile and library are both inputs to installation. Once the client starts, follow the skill path, the tool path or both, according to the task.

views.title: Select capabilities by purpose
views.description: A maintainer can start with the functional index and edit one client profile. Catalog entries also need a routing rule. The index shows the resulting availability across clients, and the installer reads the profile directly.

views.title: Install, upgrade and restore
views.description: Step 4a ends a dry run. On an actual install, follow 4b and 5. An upgrade also checks restore journals for agent settings written by an earlier installation. Step 7 is optional.

views.title: Discover skills during a session
views.description: The default install exposes core skills at launch. Each client routes workspace signals and user prompts. Explicit-only skills require a direct request, which can also activate their companion skills.

views.title: Use MCP services and language servers
views.description: Follow the MCP or LSP branch for the capability you need. OpenCode starts a configured LSP for matching files. Codex and Antigravity can provision executables and use Serena when enabled. Serena reads its own project language settings.
